items.title: Mozambique: Government and partners review lessons learned from NCRP – ADIN
items.summary: The meeting served to present an assessment of the project, discuss challenges and share lessons learned as the project closes and unfinished interventions are transferred to Moz Community, also funded by the World Bank, with a budget of US$25 million Photo: ADIN – Agência de Desenvolvimento Integrado do Norte Of the 80 infrastructure projects initially planned under the NCRP, 42 were completed during the implementation period, while the remaining interventions were transferred to Moz Community, under the leadership of the Northern Integrated Development Agency (ADIN) Photo: ADIN – Agência de Desenvolvimento Integrado do Norte On the occasion, the minister highlighted the importance of institutional coordination, compliance with procurement rules and dialogue with the business sector to improve the implementation of development projects The meeting also provided an opportunity to gather contributions from businesspeople in Cabo Delgado on the participation of local companies and the implementation and supervision of works.

items.title: Mozambique: INAM warns of strong winds
items.summary: It states that gusts of strong winds could reach up to 80 kilometres per hour south of the 25th parallel It adds that the atmospheric conditions could roughen the sea and generate waves up to five metres high, affecting maritime navigation Additionally, showers and thunderstorms are expected across the coastal districts of the country’s southern region. INAM recommends taking precautionary and safety measures for maritime navigation

items.title: Can diplomacy stop another Ethiopia-Eritrea war?
items.summary: Ethiopia has installed a new administration in conflict-hit Tigray after federal forces pushed back Tigrayan fighters. But tensions with Eritrea continue to raise fears of a wider regional war Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has announced an interim government in the country's northern Tigray region, giving it six months to prepare for regional elections and restore stability Abiy's announcement on Friday followed a military offensive launched in September by the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and six other armed groups.

items.title: Terrorists increasingly targeting civilians in three Cabo Delgado districts – ACLED
items.summary: Maputo, 19 Oct (AIM) – Islamic State Mozambique (ISM) has increasingly targeted civilians in the districts of Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe, and Macomia, in the southern Mozambican province of Cabo Delgado over the months of August and September. According to the latest report carried out by the independent conflict registration project ACLED (Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project), the terrorists have been tightening security measures in Mocimboa da Praia, constraining commercial and humanitarian activity. “As a result, the town is likely to become tense. That tension may be directed toward the state, either through protests or increased collaboration with ISM. Evidence suggests that ISM’s return to Nangade is to draw on support from neighboring Tanzania, a development likely to lead to tightened security measures on both sides of the border”, reads the report. Meanwhile, the early October release of hostages taken by ISM in Niassa province last month in return for ransom is likely to embolden the group to target foreigners for abduction in the future.
